title: Register Equality Preserves Program Semantics
statement: Let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, $B$ a natural number, $l$ a program label, $σ,σ'$ register states, and $P$ a proposition. If $σ=σ'$ and, starting at $l$ with register state $σ'$, every computation terminates with all registers bounded by $B$ at every preterminal configuration satisfying the program’s safety conditions, and an accepting computation exists exactly when $P$ holds, then the same properties hold starting at $l$ with register state $σ$.
hypotheses_covered: The abstract program semantics from $(l,σ')$ satisfies the bound and safety guard at every preterminal step and terminates for every sequence of choices
replaced:
Let $x$ be a finite bit string, $B$ a natural number, $l$ a control label,
$[1mσ,σ'[0m$ register records, and $P$ a proposition. If $σ=σ'$ and, from control
label $l$ with register record $σ'$, every sequence of choices terminates while all
registers remain at most $B$, with an accepting computation existing exactly when $P$
holds, then the same is true from $l$ with register record $σ$.
